Tom —

Appreciate the clear asks and the PO draft. High level proposal below so you can share with procurement/finance:

1) List discount: 25% off published list, 12-month term (can discuss multi-year later).
2) Accelerator credit: $100,000 applied as an invoice credit, amortized over the first 3 invoices (we can also apply as one upfront invoice credit if your accounting prefers).
3) Channel commission: Redwood can route a partner pass-through to CloudBridge. Standard approach is to pay the partner via outbound invoice (Redwood issues to CloudBridge) or route commission as a contra-revenue allocation on the private offer. Operationally the neatest for AWS is: private offer lists the net price, Redwood issues a monthly commission invoice to CloudBridge for X% of usage.

Questions for you:
- Do you prefer upfront commission vs monthly payouts?
- Can you confirm CloudBridge's finance contact and their AWS reseller account ID?

I've attached a preliminary pricing sheet and our private offer template so your legal/procurement can see the mechanics. Ben and Irene looped in to advise on commission cadence and marketplace constraints.

Next steps:
- Confirm partner payout cadence and reseller ID
- Proc sends PO back with preferred invoicing terms
- Redwood legal circulates private offer T&Cs for sign/DocuSign

Tom — quick follow on from ops/legal perspective: 

- Marketplace listing: AWS requires the private offer to be accepted by the buyer and then the seller to publish the offer in the marketplace catalog; in our experience the minimum lead time is ~5 business days after acceptance for CA/US regions.
- Commission cadence: two common patterns we use:
  * Upfront commission (one-time payment) followed by a quarterly true-up to reconcile actuals, or
  * Monthly partner invoice for actual consumption, followed by a year-end true-up.

Operational constraint to flag: if CloudBridge wants the commission paid out of marketplace payouts (i.e., deducted at source), that requires specific reseller setup with AWS and can add 2-3 weeks. Simpler path is Redwood issues a commission invoice to CloudBridge monthly.

Proposed internal ops default for this deal (we can make an exception if you need otherwise): 10% upfront commission paid to partner within 30 days of first invoice, then quarterly true-up not to exceed 12% total. If GreenWave prefers a different split, note now and we’ll flag to finance.

Attaching a simple commission schedule for your review.

Attachment: commission_schedule.csv

Thanks,

Confirming operational plan from Redwood Finance: 

- Commission: We can do 8% upfront to CloudBridge within 30 days of Redwood's first invoice, plus a 2% quarterly true-up (paid quarterly) not to exceed a 12% cumulative commission. Please provide CloudBridge's invoicing email (you indicated finance@cloudbridge.com) and their AWS reseller account ID so we can include them in the private offer metadata.

- Accelerator credit: Redwood will apply the $100,000 accelerator credit as a contra-invoice credit spread across the first three invoices (equivalent monthly reduction by default). If GreenWave requires a single-line upfront credit on your PO, we'll accept that and apply as a one-time invoice credit.

- Marketplace listing timeline: Once the private offer is accepted and the PO is submitted, typical listing publication in AWS takes 5-7 business days for US regions. If you need earlier, we can prioritize but it requires expedited legal sign-off and a cutover window.
